info.title: Acta API
info.description:
Acta's operator API, the one the dashboard uses. Lists page by cursor: pass a page's nextCursor back as cursor until hasMore is false; a cursor is tied to its query. Every POST, PUT, and DELETE is a control, mapped only where the host enables controls. A control whose request object is optional acts with its defaults when the request has no body, with or without a JSON content type. A signal raise takes any JSON value instead, and no bytes raise a presence-only signal. POST /jobs answers 201 when it inserted the job and 200 when a deduplication key matched an existing one, with the job's URL in Location either way. A string carrying x-acta-known-values is an open set: compare against the known values and keep any other value as it is. The document declares no security scheme: the host adds its own authentication, which a client sends as the host asks. Each operation names the permission it needs in x-acta-permission; where the host turns permission checks on, a call with no credential answers 401, and one whose caller lacks the permission answers 403.

A call that changes something must show that it is no cross-site form post, in one of three ways: the header X-Acta-Control: true, a JSON content type, or a Bearer authorization header. A client that sends a JSON body or a bearer token passes without doing anything more; for a call with no body and no bearer token, send the header.

get.description:
A JSON payload is the body as application/json. Any other format is application/octet-stream with its format id in X-Acta-Payload-Format, and so is a stored JSON payload that is not one strict JSON value, with format id 1.

Needs the acta.read permission.

AlertDeliveryStatusCode.description:
Where an alert stands with its delivery to its channel.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert delivery status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Raised; awaiting the first send attempt.
- retry-after: Send deferred until the alert's retryAfterUtc.
- suppressed: Intentionally not sent: the channel's policy on the sending process rejected delivery.
- delivered: Sent to the channel's transport.
- failed: Send attempt failed and the retry path is done with it; re-sent as a reminder while the incident stays unresolved.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertKindCode.description:
What condition an alert reports.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- first-failure: The failure that opened the incident: an attempt failed and the job lives on.
- threshold-reached: A counted condition reached its configured threshold, such as a job that keeps losing its claim.
- final-failure: The job failed for good.
- manual: Raised by a job's handler.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertOriginCode.description:
How an alert came to be raised.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert origin not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- automatic: Raised by the engine on a failure, a timeout, a lost worker, or a deadline.
- manual: Raised by a job's handler.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertProfileCode.description:
When the engine raises alerts for a definition's jobs on its own.

Known values:
- none: No automatic failure alerts. An alert a handler raises is still created.
- on-failure: The default. Alerts on every failed or orphaned attempt; repeats collapse onto the job's one open incident, and the final failure raises a separate alert. Every enabled profile records the attempts its alerts read, whatever the event recording level. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- info: Informational alerts on a final failure only, at low severity. A permanent slot rarely reaches one; see on-terminal. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- on-terminal: Alerts on a final failure only: the retry budget is spent, the handler failed the job, an exception is not retryable, a step that runs at most once was interrupted, or a lost lease spent the budget. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success. A deadline cancels the job and so alerts under no profile. A permanent slot never spends a budget, so use on-failure to hear about its failures.
- sys-critical: Reserved for Acta's own system jobs. Alerts at critical severity to the job's channel, or to the channel named default when the job declares none.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertRef.description: An alert's public reference: alr_ followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUID, such as alr_01a14f5038c17d0e9b2f6a4c81d3e5f7. An incident keeps its ref while it is open: a condition that fires again gets no new one.

AlertSeverityCode.description:
How severe an alert is.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert severity not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- info: Informational; not meant to page.
- warning: An attempt failed and the job lives on; repeats collapse onto the one open incident.
- error: A final failure, or an event that needs an operator's attention.
- critical: The highest severity: raised by Acta's own system jobs, or by a handler that asks for it. Whether it pages depends on the channel it is routed to.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

CheckpointKindCode.description:
What a checkpoint holds: one of the durable values a job keeps between attempts. Names are separate for each kind, so a variable never collides with a signal or a child latch of the same name.

Known values:
- unspecified: Checkpoint kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- variable: A variable a handler sets; the last write wins.
- signal: A signal; pending while awaited, set once raised.
- timer: A durable sleep timer; pending until due, consumed when the handler runs again past the due time.
- progress: The job's progress, one per job; the last write wins.
- child-latch: The latch a parent job holds for one child's outcome; pending while awaited, set when the child ends.
- firing: The record of one scheduled firing of a permanent slot or of a per-occurrence job; pending while outstanding, then settled with the outcome. It survives a handler's state reset.

CheckpointStatusCode.description:
Where a checkpoint that has a status stands. A signal or child latch is pending until it is set or its wait expires; a timer is pending until it is consumed; a firing is pending until it succeeds, fails, or is cancelled. Variables and progress have no status.

Known values:
- unspecified: Checkpoint status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Awaited or armed; the checkpoint has not been satisfied yet.
- set: Raised; the payload is stored and a waiting job proceeds.
- expired: The wait ran past its timeout and was settled as timed out; a raise after that skips it.
- consumed: The due time was reached; the handler ran again, consumed the timer, and proceeded.
- succeeded: The firing settled successfully; it stays the slot's last outcome until the next firing replaces it.
- failed: The firing settled as a final failure; it stays the slot's last outcome until the next firing replaces it.
- cancelled: The firing settled by cancellation; it stays the slot's last outcome until the next firing replaces it.

EventCode.description:
What an event records, as a dotted code. There is no code for an enqueue, because the job row itself records it.

Known values:
- unspecified: Event code not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- tenant.suspended: An operator suspended a tenant; enqueues that name it are rejected. The message carries the reason.
- tenant.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended tenant; enqueues that name it are accepted again. The message carries the reason.
- tenant.updated: An operator changed a tenant's display name or description. The message carries the reason.
- namespace.suspended: An operator suspended a namespace; enqueues into it are rejected. The message carries the reason.
- namespace.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended namespace; enqueues into it are accepted again. The message carries the reason.
- namespace.updated: An operator changed a namespace's owner team or description. The message carries the reason.
- definition.overrides-updated: An operator changed a job definition's policy overrides; the message summarizes the change.
- definition.retired: An operator retired a job definition; enqueues are rejected and its waiting jobs were cancelled.
- job.execution-succeeded: The attempt's handler returned successfully; durationMs is set. Recorded for every success under audit, under failures only for a success after counted failures, and under an enabled alert profile also for a one-shot job's success past its first attempt.
- job.execution-failed: The attempt failed and the job lives on: a retry within budget, or a permanent slot's firing that spent its budget and returned the slot to idle. durationMs and the failure's message are set; the details carry the keys reason and to.
- job.execution-orphaned: The lease of the attempt's worker expired and crash recovery reclaimed the job without ending it. workerRef names the worker that held it; the details carry the keys reason and to.
- job.execution-yielded: The attempt ended without succeeding or failing: rescheduled, suspended, paused, or cancelled by its handler or the engine. Recorded under audit only; the details carry the keys outcome and reason.
- job.failed: The job failed for good: its retry budget is spent, its handler failed it, or its failure is not retryable. durationMs is set when an attempt ran; the details carry the key reason.
- job.suspended: The attempt stopped on a durable wait: a sleep timer made the job ready again at its due time, or a wait on a signal or on child jobs left it suspended. It spends no retry budget; the details carry the key to.
- job.rescheduled: The job became ready with a new nextRunAtUtc: its handler rescheduled it, a failed attempt retries within budget, or an operator rescheduled it. The details carry the key actor or reason.
- job.cancelled: The job was cancelled, which is final.
- job.paused: The job was paused.
- job.resumed: The job was resumed: it is ready again, idle for a permanent slot with no firing outstanding, or blocked behind its lane. Crash recovery records the same event, with the reason lane-repaired in its details, when it releases the next job of a stranded lane.
- job.restarted: The job was restarted: it is ready again, idle for a permanent slot, or blocked behind its lane. Its failure count is reset and its retention cleared, and its execution number carries on.
- job.reprioritized: An operator changed the job's priority; the message carries the operator's reason, if any.
- job.purged: An operator deleted a finished job's record; the event is about the deleted job's id, and its details keep the job's jobRef, correlationKey, and actor. Recorded whatever the event recording level.
- job.input-amended: An operator replaced a job's stored input; the details carry the actor and the format name and byte count of the previous input, and the message carries the reason.
- job.signal-raised: A signal was raised for the job. Its signal checkpoint is set, unless the wait had already expired: then nothing changes, and the message says so.
- job.state-reset: The handler reset the job's state: its checkpoints and steps were cleared so the next execution starts as new. The record of a scheduled firing stays.
- job.note-recorded: A note the application's handler wrote. It is the only event an application can write, and the engine never writes it, so every other event is the engine's own. The message carries the line; the details carry the optional payload.
- schedule.paused: A recurring schedule was paused; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.resumed: A recurring schedule was resumed; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.pause-expired: A timed pause ended and the scheduler resumed the schedule. The details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.triggered: An operator fired the schedule's job by hand; the schedule's own timing did not move. The details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.admitted: The scheduler chose one of the schedule's occurrences to fire; the details carry the schedule, the occurrence, the time through which the schedule is decided, and the firing id.
- schedule.skipped: A range of the schedule's occurrences was decided without work: the misfire policy skipped it, it expired, the schedule was full, its calendar no longer produces it, or a calendar publication discarded it; details carry the schedule, the range, and the reason.
- schedule.retimed: A deploy changed the schedule's timing, or a calendar it names was published; the undecided occurrences of the old timing were discarded and the schedule continues from the first occurrence of the new one. The details carry the schedule name.
- calendar.draft-saved: An operator saved a new draft version of a catalog calendar. The details carry the calendar, the version, and the role; the message carries the reason.
- calendar.published: An operator published a catalog calendar version, which became the family's current one. Details carry the calendar, the version, the version it replaced, the overdue decision, and the schedules it affected.
- calendar.archived: An operator archived a catalog calendar's current version; the family has no current version until another is published. Details carry the calendar and the version.
- worker.started: A worker process registered and is active.
- worker.stopped: A worker process shut down cleanly.
- worker.died: A worker's heartbeat went stale and crash recovery marked it dead.
- alert.acknowledged: An operator acknowledged an alert; the message carries the note.
- alert.resolved: An operator resolved an alert by hand; the message carries the note.
- outbox.requeued: An operator returned quarantined outbox rows to delivery; the message carries the reason and the row ids.
- outbox.discarded: An operator deleted quarantined outbox rows; the message carries the reason and the deleted row ids.

JobKindCode.description:
What a job is: an ordinary job, or the one permanent slot a scheduled definition fires through. The kind is set when the job is created and never changes.

Known values:
- unspecified: Job kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ordinary: A job enqueued by an application, an operator, or a parent job's handler, or created by a schedule for one occurrence; it ends in a final status.
- permanent-slot: The one reusable job of a scheduled definition: registering the definition creates it, every firing of the definition's schedules runs through it, and it never ends by itself.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

json.description: A JSON payload, embedded as the JSON value itself: any JSON value, null included. Beside base64 a null here counts as left out.

base64.description: A payload in any other format, base64-encoded.

formatId.description: The payload format's id. Beside base64 it is required: 2 for bytes, or 128 to 255 for an application's own. Beside json it is left out, or is 1.

JobPayloadBody.description: A payload as a request carries it inside a JSON body: exactly one of json, a JSON payload as the value itself, and base64, a payload in any other format beside its formatId.

JobPriorityCode.description:
A job's priority. A worker always claims the highest priority first, with no aging, so keep bulk work in a namespace of its own.

Known values:
- bulk: Lowest practical priority; bulk-class workloads.
- normal: Default priority. Most jobs use this.
- high: Above normal; operator opt-in for time-sensitive work.
- critical: Critical priority; close-to-realtime operator workloads.
- realtime: Highest priority.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

JobRef.description: A job's public reference: job_ followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUID, such as job_01a14f4e954e7bf68ac609f3fcad8e3d. Every API addresses a job by it. It copies and searches as one word, and reads in creation order.

JobStatusCode.description:
Where a job is in its life.

Known values:
- unspecified: Job status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ready: Waiting for a worker to claim it.
- blocked: Waiting behind an earlier unfinished job of its lane; no worker is offered it, and it becomes ready when the job ahead ends.
- suspended: Stopped until something outside the attempt happens: a signal its handler waits for, or the end of child jobs it waits on.
- paused: Not running until it is resumed.
- idle: A permanent slot between firings, with nothing outstanding and no lease. A firing makes it ready; it never ends by itself.
- executing: Claimed by a worker under a live lease; its handler is running or about to start.
- succeeded: Ended successfully.
- failed: Ended in failure: its attempts are spent, an exception is not retryable, a step that runs at most once was interrupted, or its handler failed it.
- cancelled: Ended by cancellation: by an operator, a caller, or its own handler, by a strict deadline, or because its definition was retired.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

MisfireStrategyCode.description:
What a schedule does about occurrences it missed during downtime.

Known values:
- unspecified: Misfire strategy not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- catch-up-once: After downtime, fire once immediately for all missed occurrences, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- skip: After downtime, skip all missed occurrences and resume from the first occurrence strictly after now.
- catch-up-latest: After downtime, fire once for the latest missed occurrence, the earlier ones coalesced into it, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- catch-up-all: After downtime, fire every missed occurrence in order, one per settlement, subject to the schedule's capacity.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduledDeliveryCode.description:
How a schedule delivers a definition's work: one permanent slot job fired again and again, or a fresh root job per admitted occurrence. Immutable once the definition is registered.

Known values:
- unspecified: Scheduled delivery not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- permanent: Default. The definition's schedules fire one permanent slot job again and again.
- per-occurrence: Each admitted occurrence enqueues a fresh ordinary root job with its own state, retries, and retention.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleEvaluationStatusCode.description:
Why a schedule's next evaluation is when it is: where the scheduling engine stands with one schedule, apart from the schedule's own status and from the status of the job it fires.

Known values:
- unspecified: Evaluation status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- scheduled: The next evaluation is the next nominal occurrence, or the end of a timed pause.
- waiting-for-capacity: An occurrence is due but the permanent slot is busy or the schedule is at its limit of outstanding occurrences; it fires when one of them ends.
- exhausted: The schedule has no further occurrence; a change to its declaration or to its calendar reactivates it.
- evaluation-error: The schedule's expression or calendar could not be evaluated; the schedule keeps its place and the evaluation retries after a bounded delay.
- slot-unavailable: An occurrence is due but the permanent slot is held, cancelled, or failed terminally; a job resume or restart wakes it.
- resumed: An operator resumed the schedule; its first evaluation decides the backlog under the misfire policy and expires the stale part without pausing again.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleExpireActionCode.description:
What happens to an occurrence that reaches its schedule's expiry before it is admitted.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule expire action not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- discard: An occurrence older than the schedule's expiry when it is evaluated is skipped, audited with the reason expired, and the schedule moves on.
- pause: An occurrence older than the schedule's expiry when it is evaluated is skipped, audited with the reason expired, and the schedule is paused with the reason until an operator resumes it.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleExpressionKindCode.description:
What kind of expression a schedule has.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule expression kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- cron: A cron expression.
- interval: An interval, in short form such as 5m or in ISO 8601 such as PT5M or P1D.
- calendar: A calendar the expression names; the schedule's occurrences come from that calendar.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleFullBehaviorCode.description:
What a due occurrence does when its schedule already has its maximum of unsettled occurrences.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule full behavior not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- wait: Default. An occurrence of a full schedule stays undecided until a settlement frees capacity.
- drop: An occurrence of a full schedule is skipped, audited, and the schedule moves on.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleOriginCode.description:
Where a schedule came from.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule origin not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- operator: Added by an operator. Nothing creates a schedule of this origin today.
- definition: Declared in the application's code, and refreshed when the application registers its definitions.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleStatusCode.description:
Where a schedule is in its life.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: The schedule fires.
- paused: Paused, by an operator or by the engine under a firing failure policy or an expiry action; it does not fire until it is resumed, or until pausedUntilUtc passes when that is set.
- orphaned: The application's code no longer declares the schedule; it cannot fire, be paused, or be resumed.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

StepStatusCode.description:
Where a step stands. A step is pending from its first start and across retries, and ends succeeded, exhausted when its retries are spent, or interrupted when a step that runs at most once was re-entered before it completed.

Known values:
- unspecified: Step status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Running, or waiting to retry within its retry budget.
- succeeded: Completed; its result, when it has one, is stored.
- exhausted: Its retries are spent; the job's handler receives the failure.
- interrupted: A step that runs at most once was re-entered before it completed, so whether it ran is unknown; the job's handler receives the interruption.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

jobRef.description: The ref of the job the call fired: a new job on a per-occurrence schedule, the permanent slot's job on a permanent one; null unless the call was applied.

TriggerScheduleResponse.description: What firing a schedule once now did, and the schedule's state after the attempt. It works for both delivery modes and never moves the schedule's cadence. Applied means a job was made ready, not that it ran. Calls are not deduplicated: a retry after a lost response admits a second job on a per-occurrence schedule, while a permanent slot rejects it until the slot is idle again.

description.description: A note for operators; it changes nothing the calendar computes.

of.description: The operands, each a definition of the family's role, written inline.

UnionCalendar.description: The union of calendars of the family's role: an availability union is open whenever one of its operands is, and an occurrence union fires at every instant one of its operands does.

expectedVersion.description: The version as the caller last read it; when the row has another version the call answers version-conflict and changes nothing.

overrides.description: The whole set of overrides to store, every member present: null clears that override, and a body that leaves a member out answers 400.

reasonMessage.description: Why the operator made this call, recorded on the event the call writes.

UpdateDefinitionOverridesRequest.description: Body of the override update: the version the operator last read, and the whole set of overrides, which replaces the stored one.

action.description: What the call did: applied; version-conflict, when the expected version is stale; or not-found.

version.description: The definition's version after the call; on a version conflict, the version it has now; null when the definition was not found.

UpdateDefinitionOverridesResponse.description: What setting a definition's policy overrides did, and the definition's version after the attempt.

input.description: The input to give the job, as a payload envelope.

reasonMessage.description: Why the operator made this call, recorded on the event the call writes.

UpdateJobInputRequest.description: Body of PUT /jobs/{jobRef}/input: the payload envelope that replaces the job's input, required. A json input replaces any stored format; base64 replaces only a binary-format input, and its formatId is the stored one.

action.description: What the call did: applied; rejected, when the job is executing or has no input to replace; or not-found.

status.description: The job's status after the call; null when the job was not found or has no input to replace.

UpdateJobInputResponse.description: What updating a job's input did, and the job's status after the attempt; the update carries no version.

ownerTeam.description: The team that owns the namespace; omitted or null stores none.

description.description: The namespace's description; omitted or null stores none.

expectedVersion.description: The version as the caller last read it; when the row has another version the call answers version-conflict and changes nothing.

reasonMessage.description: Why the operator made this call, recorded on the event the call writes.

UpdateNamespaceRequest.description: Body of the namespace update, which replaces its owner team and description: a member left out or null is cleared.

action.description: What the call did: applied; version-conflict, when the expected version is stale; or not-found.

version.description: The namespace's version after the call; on a version conflict, the version it has now; null when the namespace was not found.

UpdateNamespaceResponse.description: What updating a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

description.description: The tenant's description; omitted or null stores none.

expectedVersion.description: The version as the caller last read it; when the row has another version the call answers version-conflict and changes nothing.

reasonMessage.description: Why the operator made this call, recorded on the event the call writes.

UpdateTenantRequest.description: Body of the tenant update, which replaces its display name and description: a member left out or null is cleared.

action.description: What the call did: applied; version-conflict, when the expected version is stale; or not-found.

version.description: The tenant's version after the call; on a version conflict, the version it has now; null when the tenant was not found.

UpdateTenantResponse.description: What updating a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

value.description: The tag's value; null for a tag that is only a name.

UpsertTagRequest.description: Body of PUT .../tags/{tagName} on a job, a namespace, a tenant, or a definition: the tag's optional value. The name is the route's, normalized as every tag name is.

action.description: What the call did: applied, or not-found.

UpsertTagResponse.description: What upserting one tag did: applied, or the target did not exist.

description.description: A note for operators; it changes nothing the calendar computes.

timeZone.description: The zone the local times are in: a time zone id the host knows, such as Europe/Ljubljana, or schedule for the zone of the schedule that uses the calendar, which is also what leaving it out means.

weekly.description: The weekly rules; the windows of every rule that names a weekday apply on it.

dateOverrides.description: Dates whose windows replace the weekly ones, keyed by the date as yyyy-MM-dd; an empty list closes the date.

excludedRanges.description: Ranges cut out of the windows after everything else is applied.

WeeklyAvailabilityCalendar.description: An availability calendar of weekly windows in local time, with single dates overridden and ranges cut out. It needs at least one weekly rule or date override.

WorkerRef.description: A worker's public reference: wrk_ followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUID, such as wrk_01a14f4d7b2a7c4f8e1d3b5a6c7e9f01. Each start of a worker process gets a new one.

WorkerStatusCode.description:
Where a worker process is in its life.

Known values:
- unspecified: Worker status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Claiming and running jobs.
- draining: Claiming no more jobs; finishing the ones it runs.
- stopped: Shut down cleanly.
- dead: Its heartbeat went stale; crash recovery reclaims its expired leases, and a heartbeat that resumes makes it active again.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.
